                                                                        Help CenterScheduling MessagesCan I Edit a Scheduled Post After Scheduling It?

                                                                        Can I Edit a Scheduled Post After Scheduling It?

                                                                        Scheduling Messages3 Q&A

                                                                        Nothing about a scheduled post is carved in stone. Until the moment Telegram accepts the send, every part of it can change — that is the whole point of keeping a queue instead of posting immediately.

                                                                        What you can change

                                                                        • Text and formatting — fix a typo, rewrite the hook, add links. Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, spoilers and code all survive edits.
                                                                        • Media — swap the image, replace the video, add or remove an album item.
                                                                        • Send time — move the post earlier or later, or to another day entirely.
                                                                        • Target channel — re-point a post to a different connected channel.

                                                                        Open the Message List (or /list), tap the post, choose 🔄 Replace. The familiar schedule flow reopens with the post's current content pre-filled — change what you need and confirm.

                                                                        What editing cannot do

                                                                        • Change a post that already published. Once the sender bot delivers the message to Telegram, it is a normal Telegram message — edit it with Telegram's own tools, not here.
                                                                        • Edit recurring posts “in place”. A recurring rule is a single template that fires on its pattern — there are no separate per-day copies. Edit the rule so all future sends change.

                                                                        A workflow that actually works

                                                                        Channel operators who stay sane usually: schedule the week on Sunday, review the Calendar Monday, and treat edit as the normal verb — improving copy as the news moves. Edits are free, instant, and never notify subscribers. The only deadline is the send time itself.

                                                                        Common questions

                                                                        How late can I edit a post?

                                                                        Any time before the send moment. If the bot is mid-delivery, the edit may not apply — that is the only race. For a post due within seconds, delete and reschedule instead.

                                                                        Edit Messages
                                                                        Can I edit a post that already went out?

                                                                        Not from the bot — it is a regular Telegram message now. Telegram itself lets admins edit posted messages in channels; use Telegram for that.

                                                                        Delete Messages
                                                                        Does editing reset the monthly send counter?

                                                                        No. The counter counts actual sends, not edits. Editing costs nothing.

                                                                        How to Schedule Many Telegram Posts at Once (Bulk Workflow)

                                                                        Scheduling Messages2 Q&A

                                                                        Scheduling one post at a time is fine for a meme; for a content calendar you want batch workflows. Fast Scheduler gives you three, and a full week can be set up in minutes.

                                                                        Way 1 — import a batch with SetDate

                                                                        The SetDate bot is the bulk tool: prepare messages as a set (text, times), then import them into Fast Scheduler in one click. It shines when you write copy in advance or migrate from another scheduler. Prepare → import → review in the Message List → done.

                                                                        Way 2 — let recurring rules do the repeating

                                                                        Anything that repeats should be a rule, not N one-off posts: “every day at 9:00”, “Mondays 18:30”, “every 6 hours”. Premium users get unlimited rules and no expiry; Free has one rule. Combined with a signature, a daily digest literally runs itself.

                                                                        Way 3 — stock the queue ahead

                                                                        The queue lets you stack up to 100 pending posts on Free (unlimited on Premium). The classic pattern: one writing session → schedule the whole week → check the Calendar view for holes and collisions → go live your life. Edits are free and instant, so the queue is your draft folder as much as your pipeline.

                                                                        Checking your work

                                                                        Three tools keep bulk work honest:

                                                                        • Calendar — month at a glance; tap a day to see that day's posts.
                                                                        • Message List — per-channel queue with previews; catch same-time twins here.
                                                                        • Search — keyword search across everything scheduled, with per-result preview and edit for cleanup.

                                                                        Common questions

                                                                        Is there a true “upload a CSV of posts” feature?

                                                                        Close: SetDate handles prepared batches, and /import accepts .json/.csv/.txt/.rtf/.odt files of messages. For calendar-scale bulk entry, SetDate is the intended tool.

                                                                        SetDate IntegrationSupported Import Formats
                                                                        How far ahead can I schedule?

                                                                        As far as your queue limit allows — up to 100 pending posts on Free, unlimited on Premium. Times years out are fine.

                                                                        Help CenterScheduling MessagesHow to Automate Recurring Posts in Telegram (Daily Digests, Weekly Roundups)

                                                                        How to Automate Recurring Posts in Telegram (Daily Digests, Weekly Roundups)

                                                                        Scheduling Messages2 Q&A

                                                                        Anything your channel repeats should never be scheduled by hand twice. Recurring rules encode the pattern once — “daily at 9:00”, “every Monday 18:30”, “every 6 hours” — and the bot keeps generating posts on time, forever (or until the rule expires).

                                                                        Creating a rule

                                                                        • 1. Tap 🔄 Recurring Messages in the bot (or send /recurring) and follow the flow.
                                                                        • 2. Compose the message — text, media, the works — exactly like a normal post.
                                                                        • 3. Pick the pattern: daily, weekly (with weekday picker), or custom interval.
                                                                        • 4. Set the time in the channel's time zone and confirm.

                                                                        The rule's future posts expand in the Calendar like any others, and the rule itself is listed with your recurring messages — so there is always a truthful picture of what will publish.

                                                                        Expiry — the part people forget

                                                                        On Free, the single recurring rule runs for 365 days, then expires with a notice — create a new rule to continue. It is the anti-zombie mechanism: dead rules can't silently post forever. Premium rules never expire, and you can run unlimited rules — one per content type is the usual pattern.

                                                                        Patterns that work in real channels

                                                                        • Daily digest — a template message (“Top 3 of the day”) with the signature carrying credit; edit the rule weekly, not daily.
                                                                        • Weekly roundup — Monday 9:00 rule; combine with the calendar to dodge holidays.
                                                                        • Scheduled reminders — every-6-hours service posts for community managers; Premium's unlimited rules shine here.

                                                                        Editing and stopping

                                                                        Rules are editable — change text, time, or pattern, and future instances follow. Pause or delete when a campaign ends. Deleting a rule never deletes already-posted messages.

                                                                        Common questions

                                                                        Why did my recurring rule stop working?

                                                                        On Free, rules expire after 365 days and you get an expiry notice — create a new rule to continue. Premium rules never expire. Also check the sender bot is still admin — a failed delivery stops the chain.

                                                                        Recurring MessagesScheduled Message Didn’t Post? The 6 Real Causes, In Order of Likelihood
                                                                        Can two rules post at the same time?

                                                                        Yes, and they will — in the order created. If they are too close together, Telegram may throttle the burst; space rules by a few minutes.

                                                                        Help CenterScheduling MessagesWhat Types of Content Can You Schedule With Fast Scheduler?

                                                                        What Types of Content Can You Schedule With Fast Scheduler?

                                                                        Scheduling Messages3 Q&A

                                                                        A scheduling bot is only as good as the content it can carry. Fast Scheduler handles the full Telegram media palette, so your editorial plans never have to shrink to fit the tool.

                                                                        Everything you can attach to a scheduled post

                                                                        • Photos — compressed automatically for fast delivery without visible quality loss.
                                                                        • Videos — including size limits that scale with your plan (up to 25MB on Free, up to 50MB on Premium).
                                                                        • Video notes (round videos) and voice messages.
                                                                        • Audio files — full tracks with cover art preserved.
                                                                        • Documents — PDFs, archives, anything Telegram accepts.
                                                                        • Animations — GIFs and MP4 loops.
                                                                        • Stickers — from any of your packs.
                                                                        • Polls and quizzes — scheduled like any other post.
                                                                        • Locations and venues — supported for per-post content.

                                                                        Albums and media groups

                                                                        Multiple photos or videos sent together are scheduled as one album and publish as a single media group — exactly how your followers expect it. You can also build a randomized pool: attach a mix of photos, videos, documents or any files and let the scheduler pick one per send, which is perfect for daily wallpaper or quote channels where variety matters.

                                                                        Text always travels with media

                                                                        Captions keep their formatting (bold, italic, links, spoilers) and your configured signature is appended to media posts as well. Inline URL buttons attach to media posts too, so a “Read more” button under a photo works out of the box.

                                                                        Limits that matter

                                                                        • Max media size: up to 10 MB on Free, 100 MB on Premium.
                                                                        • Videos: up to 25MB on Free, up to 50MB on Premium.
                                                                        • Media Storage boxes: 1 box with 100 items total on Free — Premium raises this to 20 boxes with 500 items total across the account, so reusable assets live in the bot instead of your camera roll.

                                                                        Anything Telegram itself refuses (for example, a corrupted file) is rejected at scheduling time with a clear message — never discovered silently on the day of publishing.

                                                                        Common questions

                                                                        Can I schedule Telegram polls with Fast Scheduler?

                                                                        Yes. Polls and quizzes are scheduled like any other message and publish through your sender bot at the set time.

                                                                        Scheduling FAQ
                                                                        Can I schedule an album of photos?

                                                                        Yes. Photos and videos sent together are scheduled as one media group. You can also attach a pool of mixed files and let the scheduler pick one randomly per send.

                                                                        Media Storage
                                                                        What is the maximum video size for scheduled messages?

                                                                        Videos up to 25MB on the Free plan and up to 50MB with Premium, in line with Telegram bots own upload limits.

                                                                        Help CenterScheduling MessagesHow Do I Format Telegram Posts? (Bold, Italic, Links, Spoilers and Buttons)

                                                                        How Do I Format Telegram Posts? (Bold, Italic, Links, Spoilers and Buttons)

                                                                        Scheduling Messages3 Q&A

                                                                        Formatting is what separates a channel that looks professional from one that looks like a group chat. Fast Scheduler keeps every bit of it intact between scheduling and publishing.

                                                                        Rich text survives the whole pipeline

                                                                        Write a message anywhere — bold headlines, italic asides, underlined warnings, struck-through corrections, monospace code — and schedule it. Formatting is stored as Telegram entities, not flat text, so what publishes is pixel-identical to what you wrote: no mangled asterisks, no lost links, no broken emoji.

                                                                        Spoilers

                                                                        Wrap part of the text in spoiler markup and it publishes as a real Telegram spoiler — blurred until a reader taps it. Perfect for giveaways, answers, and sensitive details. The bot validates spoiler markup while you type, so unclosed pairs are caught at scheduling time, not in front of your audience.

                                                                        Inline URL buttons

                                                                        Add tappable buttons to any post with one syntax: [Button Text](https://example.com). Use them for call-to-action links — “Read the guide”, “Buy now”, “Join the chat”. Buttons attach to text posts and to media posts alike. Keep button labels short (two or three words read best) and test one post before scheduling a whole campaign.

                                                                        Custom emoji

                                                                        Premium Telegram emoji in your drafts are preserved on publish, so your brand’s custom smileys do not degrade into defaults.

                                                                        Signatures: formatting that stamps itself

                                                                        Configure a signature once — a footer with your links, hashtags or contact — and every scheduled post carries it automatically, on text and media alike. Signatures keep their own formatting, and you can override the signature per post when a particular message should go out clean.

                                                                        A checklist for polished posts

                                                                        • One bold hook line first — most readers see only it in notifications.
                                                                        • Links as buttons where possible; they out-click inline links.
                                                                        • Spoilers for anything the reader should opt into.
                                                                        • A signature so every post quietly advertises your next channel.

                                                                        Common questions

                                                                        Does Telegram formatting survive scheduling in Fast Scheduler?

                                                                        Yes. Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code, links, spoilers and custom emoji are stored as Telegram entities and publish exactly as written.

                                                                        Scheduling FAQ
                                                                        How do I add buttons to a scheduled Telegram post?

                                                                        Use the syntax [Button Text](https://your-link.com) in the message. The bot converts it into a tappable inline URL button on the published post.

                                                                        Inline Buttons
                                                                        Can every scheduled post have an automatic signature?

                                                                        Yes. Create a signature once and it is appended to every scheduled and recurring post automatically, keeping its own formatting. Individual posts can override it.

                                                                        Signatures (Premium)

                                                                          Add a Channel

                                                                          Channels

                                                                          To connect a channel:
                                                                          1. Make @FastSchedulerBot an Administrator in the channel (Post Messages permission).
                                                                          2. Open the bot → Channels → Connect Channel.

                                                                              Manage Channels

                                                                              Channels

                                                                              Everything about one channel lives in two places: the Channels list and the channel's own info screen.

                                                                              Channels (main menu) lists every channel you have connected. For each channel you get:
                                                                              • The channel name.
                                                                              • Time Zone — posts for this channel are sent in the channel's own time zone, so you never juggle UTC offsets yourself.
                                                                              • Change Channel — replace this channel with a different one; its scheduled messages move with you.
                                                                              • Disconnect Channel — unlink the channel (see Remove a Channel).

                                                                              Tap a channel's → button for the details screen: connection role, sender bot, time zone, and how many scheduled and recurring messages the channel holds.

                                                                              Each channel is configured independently — ideal for multi-channel setups.

                                                                                Channel Permissions

                                                                                Channels

                                                                                For the bot to work, these admin permissions are needed:
                                                                                • Post Messages - required to send posts.
                                                                                • Edit Messages - recommended, for editing after posting.
                                                                                • Delete Messages - recommended, for cleanup.

                                                                                Add the bot as an administrator in channel settings and tick the permissions you want. Without Post Messages, scheduling will fail with a "bot is not admin" error.

                                                                                  How Posting Works: Sender Bots

                                                                                  Channels

                                                                                  Every post in your channel is delivered by a sender bot — that is what makes scheduling possible at all. This is not an optional nicety: the scheduler unlocks only after each connected channel has its own sender bot, because Telegram requires a bot to hold Post Messages rights in the channel it posts to.

                                                                                  What this means in practice
                                                                                  • Posts appear from your bot's name and avatar, not from @FastSchedulerBot — your brand stays in front of readers.
                                                                                  • One bot per channel. A second channel needs a second bot (create as many as you like in @BotFather).
                                                                                  • Free plan includes 1 sender bot; Premium raises this to 3.
                                                                                  • If a send ever fails (say, the bot lost its admin rights), Fast Scheduler retries through the main bot so the post is not lost — and warns you to restore the bot's permissions.

                                                                                  Connected a channel but not a bot yet? Open Bots → 🔑 I Have a Token and finish the pairing — scheduling, the calendar, and every other sending feature stay locked until then.

                                                                                      Unlink vs Delete

                                                                                      Channels
                                                                                      • Unlink / Remove a channel - the bot stops posting to it; its messages are paused but preserved.
                                                                                      • Delete a message - the scheduled/recurring message is removed permanently.

                                                                                      Unlinking is reversible: re-connect the channel and everything resumes. Deleting is permanent - use it only when you're sure.

                                                                                        Remove a Channel

                                                                                        Channels

                                                                                        To unlink a channel:
                                                                                        1. Open Channels → find the channel.
                                                                                        2. Tap 🔗 Disconnect Channel → confirm.

                                                                                        What happens to the channel's messages:
                                                                                        • Scheduled messages on that channel are removed or reassigned to another connected channel — the bot tells you exactly how many.
                                                                                        • Recurring messages are reassigned to another connected channel too; if none is connected, they stop.
                                                                                        • If a sender bot was attached only to this channel, the bot notifies you that it no longer has a channel to post to.

                                                                                        Re-connecting the channel later starts fresh — reconnect its sender bot before scheduling again. To delete individual messages, use Message List instead.

                                                                                          Signature

                                                                                          Channels

                                                                                          A signature is your custom footer (or header) — for example "Posted by @yourchannel" — added automatically when a post goes out.

                                                                                          How: send /signature (or tap 📝 Signature on the review screen) → create a signature with ➕ Add Signature → choose its position (start or end of the post) and how many blank lines separate it from the content. When saving you can enable auto-add and pick the channels it should attach to.

                                                                                          • Saved signatures are reusable — edit, re-position, or delete them from Saved Signatures.
                                                                                          • Signatures are attached at send time, so your stored messages stay clean.
                                                                                          • Free users can try the feature once; after that it is Premium.

                                                                                          See also: Signature Position.

                                                                                            Channel Stats

                                                                                            Channels

                                                                                            Premium users can view per-channel statistics and paginated leaderboards: top posts by views, comments, or reactions (up to 50 per page), plus a top-commentators ranking of the people who comment most on your posts.

                                                                                            Filtering: combine metric (views / comments / reactions / commentators), period (today / week / month / year / all), and page size (10 / 25 / 50) — then flip pages with the pager buttons.

                                                                                            Comment authors: to see who actually comments, add the bot to your channel's discussion group. Until then, the leaderboard shows a tip reminding you — once the bot is in the group, comments are attributed automatically.

                                                                                            These stats help you learn what content performs best so you can schedule more of what works. Channel stats are available for every connected channel — shown in the main bot, or inside its sender bot.

                                                                                              How to Connect a Telegram Channel to Fast Scheduler (Full Walkthrough)

                                                                                              Channels3 Q&A

                                                                                              Connecting a channel is a two-part handshake: the bot needs admin rights in the channel, and the channel needs to be registered in the bot. Here is the whole dance, including the steps people miss.

                                                                                              Part 1 — make the bot an admin of your channel

                                                                                              • 1. Open your channel in Telegram → Manage Channel → Administrators → Add Admin.
                                                                                              • 2. Search for @FastSchedulerBot and add it.
                                                                                              • 3. Give it at least Post Messages. If you plan to schedule on behalf of other admins or use anonymous admin, keep the defaults sane.

                                                                                              Part 2 — register the channel in the bot

                                                                                              • 1. In the bot, tap Connect Channel.
                                                                                              • 2. Give the bot what it asks for — any of these works:
                                                                                                • the channel's @username for public channels,
                                                                                                • a forwarded message from the channel,
                                                                                                • an invite link (t.me/+… or t.me/joinchat/…) for private channels.
                                                                                              • 3. Confirm. The bot verifies that it really is an admin there.

                                                                                              Part 3 — pair the sender bot (mandatory)

                                                                                              Every channel needs a sender bot — your own bot created via @BotFather — before anything can be scheduled. This is not optional: the sender bot is the account that actually publishes your posts, under its name. Fast Scheduler's main bot coordinates the schedule; the sender bot delivers. The in-bot wizard creates and pairs one in a minute; see the sender-bots guide for the detailed flow.

                                                                                              The classic errors, decoded

                                                                                              • “Channel not found” — typo in the username, or the bot was not added as admin before you tried to connect. Add first, then connect.
                                                                                              • “Not an admin” — the admin rights were granted to a different bot than the one you connected.
                                                                                              • “Invalid token” — the sender-bot token got truncated on copy. Copy the whole thing: digits, colon, the rest.

                                                                                              Common questions

                                                                                              Can I connect a private channel?

                                                                                              Yes — via invite link or by forwarding any message from the channel during connection. Public username is not required.

                                                                                              Add a Channel
                                                                                              Why do I need my own bot just to post?

                                                                                              Telegram architecture: messages in a channel are sent by a bot account, not by your user account. Pairing your own sender bot also means posts appear under your brand, not a generic one.

                                                                                              Posting as Your Bot
                                                                                              The channel connects but posts fail. First checks?

                                                                                              Sender bot still admin? Post Messages permission on? Bot not revoked in @BotFather? Those three cover nearly all post failures.

                                                                                              How Do I Connect a Private Telegram Channel to Fast Scheduler?

                                                                                              Channels3 Q&A

                                                                                              Private channels are fully supported — the bot never needs to be able to search your channel, it only needs to be inside it as an admin. There are four accepted ways to point Fast Scheduler at a private channel, and at least one of them will take you under a minute.

                                                                                              Before you start: give the bots admin rights

                                                                                              • Open your private channel → Administrators → Add Admin.
                                                                                              • Add @FastSchedulerBot with the Post Messages permission. That single permission is enough to schedule and publish.
                                                                                              • Then, inside Fast Scheduler, pair a sender bot and make it an admin of the same channel. This step is mandatory: every scheduled post is published through your sender bot, never through the main bot, so nothing in the scheduling flow unlocks until each connected channel has one.

                                                                                              Four ways to connect the channel

                                                                                              Open the bot → Channels → Connect Channel, then send whichever of these is easiest for you:

                                                                                              • @username — private channels have no @username, so this one is mostly for public channels.
                                                                                              • Forward any post from the channel to the bot. This is the fastest way for private channels: open the channel, long-press any message, Forward → Fast Scheduler Bot. The bot reads the source channel from the forward.
                                                                                              • An invite link — copy Invite Link from the channel menu and paste it into the chat.
                                                                                              • The channel ID — the numeric -100… identifier (e.g. -1001234567890) if you know it from another tool.

                                                                                              Why the invite-link and forward methods are equivalent

                                                                                              Both simply resolve your private channel to its internal ID. Fast Scheduler stores that ID plus your admin status; the channel’s privacy settings never matter again after the connection is made. You can rename the channel, change its link, or toggle “slow mode” — the connection survives all of it.

                                                                                              If connecting fails

                                                                                              • Bot is not an admin — re-check step one; the permission check runs live against Telegram.
                                                                                              • Invite link revoked or set to “join request” — regenerate the link, or forward a post instead.
                                                                                              • You are not the owner — the connector must hold admin rights in the channel under the account that talks to the bot.

                                                                                              Free plan: 1 channel. Premium raises this to 3, each with its own sender bot, time zone and statistics.

                                                                                              Common questions

                                                                                              Can Fast Scheduler post to a private channel?

                                                                                              Yes. Private channels are connected by forwarding a post from the channel, pasting an invite link, or sending the -100 channel ID. The channel being private does not affect scheduling in any way.

                                                                                              Add a Channel
                                                                                              Does the sender bot also need admin rights in a private channel?

                                                                                              Yes. The main bot needs Post Messages to verify and manage, and your sender bot needs Post Messages because it is the account that actually publishes every scheduled post.

                                                                                              Posting as Your Bot
                                                                                              How many channels can I connect on the Free plan?

                                                                                              Free includes 1 channel with 100 sent messages per month. Premium raises the limit to 3 channels with unlimited sends.

                                                                                                  Manage Sender Bots

                                                                                                  Sender Bots

                                                                                                  From Bots in the main menu you can see all connected bots and:

                                                                                                    Sender Bot Management

                                                                                                    Sender Bots

                                                                                                    A sender bot is more than a posting tool — it is also a full management interface for your channel.

                                                                                                    How it works
                                                                                                    When you connect a sender bot to a channel, management moves to it automatically — no extra setup. The main bot then shows a restricted menu (or a private "Public Mode" view if you hide the channel), while the full dashboard lives inside your bot.

                                                                                                    Inside the sender bot (Management menu)
                                                                                                    • Hide / Show Channel — in Public Mode your channel name is hidden from strangers who start the bot; they only see a generic welcome and an Open Main Bot button.
                                                                                                    • Admins — grant other Telegram accounts limited access to your channel: scheduling, viewing stats, or managing settings (RBAC).
                                                                                                    • Channel admins open the same bot and see exactly the tools their role allows — nothing more.

                                                                                                    Restore to the main bot? Not needed. Management stays with the sender bot; if the bot's token ever breaks, Fast Scheduler falls back to the main bot for delivery so posts are never lost.

                                                                                                                    Do You Need a Sender Bot to Schedule Posts? (Yes — Here Is Why)

                                                                                                                    Sender Bots3 Q&A

                                                                                                                    Short answer: yes — a sender bot is required for scheduling and sending. The scheduling menu stays locked until every connected channel has one paired. Here is the why and the 60-second setup.

                                                                                                                    Why the main bot cannot just post itself

                                                                                                                    Two reasons, one technical and one yours:

                                                                                                                    • Architecture: channel posts are delivered by a bot account with admin rights. If @FastSchedulerBot delivered them, every message on every customer channel would carry the same name — and one bot hitting rate limits would slow thousands of channels.
                                                                                                                    • Your brand: with your own sender bot, posts appear from your bot's name and avatar. Subscribers see your brand, and your bot's admin rights are yours to revoke.

                                                                                                                    Creating one in 60 seconds

                                                                                                                    • 1. Open @BotFather → /newbot → pick a name and username.
                                                                                                                    • 2. Copy the token (digits, colon, letters — the whole string).
                                                                                                                    • 3. In Fast Scheduler: Bots → ➕ Add Another Bot, pick the channel when asked, paste the token. Pairing is automatic.
                                                                                                                    • 4. Make the new bot an admin of the channel with Post Messages permission — or let Fast Scheduler promote it automatically when it can. Scheduling unlocks instantly.

                                                                                                                    The in-bot wizard walks these exact steps and checks each one, so you cannot get the order wrong.

                                                                                                                    Security, briefly

                                                                                                                    Your token is stored encrypted and used only to deliver your posts. You can rotate it any time via @BotFather (/revoke) and update it in the bot — or remove the bot entirely, which deletes the token from Fast Scheduler's storage. If a token leaks, revoke it in BotFather first; a revoked token is dead everywhere.

                                                                                                                    One bot per channel (Premium: 3×3)

                                                                                                                    Free pairs 1 sender bot with 1 channel; Premium allows 3 bots across 3 channels. Multiple channels can share one sender bot, but the clean setup — one bot per channel — keeps branding separate and failures isolated.

                                                                                                                    Common questions

                                                                                                                    Can one sender bot serve two channels?

                                                                                                                    Yes, a sender bot can be paired with multiple channels you own. One bot per channel is still recommended for cleaner branding and simpler troubleshooting.

                                                                                                                    Bot Fleet
                                                                                                                    What happens if I remove the sender bot from the channel?

                                                                                                                    Scheduling locks (no sender paired for that channel) and queued sends fail until you re-add the bot as admin. The schedules themselves stay saved.

                                                                                                                    Remove a Sender Bot
                                                                                                                    Is my bot token safe with Fast Scheduler?

                                                                                                                    Tokens are stored encrypted and never displayed in full after saving. Rotating the token in @BotFather instantly invalidates the old one everywhere.

                                                                                                                    How to Manage Your Sender Bots: Rotate, Rename, and Keep Them Healthy

                                                                                                                    Sender Bots2 Q&A

                                                                                                                    Your sender bot is the public face of every post, so a little hygiene goes a long way. Everything below lives in Sender Bots (or /bots) in Fast Scheduler.

                                                                                                                    Check status before you check anything else

                                                                                                                    The bots screen shows each bot's connection state and which channels it serves. If a send ever fails, this is the first screen: a bot showing disconnected means a revoked token or a BotFather change — fix it there, not in the schedule.

                                                                                                                    Rotating a token (the right way)

                                                                                                                    • 1. @BotFather → /mybots → your bot → Revoke current token.
                                                                                                                    • 2. Copy the new token.
                                                                                                                    • 3. Fast Scheduler → Bots → 🔁 Replace Token under the bot → paste.

                                                                                                                    The swap is instant and schedules keep running. Do it the other way around (revoke and forget) and every send fails until you paste the new token.

                                                                                                                    Rename = rebrand

                                                                                                                    A bot's public name and avatar come from @BotFather (/setname, /setuserpic) — change them there and every future post instantly carries the new look. No re-pairing needed; Fast Scheduler stores the token, not the cosmetics.

                                                                                                                    Fleet hygiene

                                                                                                                    • One bot per channel keeps branding separate and failures isolated (Premium: up to 3 bots).
                                                                                                                    • Remove bots you no longer use — removal deletes the token from storage; the bot account itself lives on in BotFather.
                                                                                                                    • After any BotFather change, glance at the status screen once — 10 seconds that prevent a silent failed-post day.

                                                                                                                    Common questions

                                                                                                                    Can I use the same bot for multiple channels?

                                                                                                                    Yes — a sender bot can serve several of your channels. Separate bots per channel remain the cleaner default for branding and debugging.

                                                                                                                    Bot Fleet
                                                                                                                    I deleted a bot in BotFather. What happens in Fast Scheduler?

                                                                                                                    Its sends fail with an invalid-token error and the status screen shows it disconnected. Remove the bot from Sender Bots and pair a replacement.

                                                                                                                    Remove a Sender Bot

                                                                                                                    Admins

                                                                                                                    Admins4 Q&A

                                                                                                                    The Admins section manages who can use a connected channel and what they can do. It lives inside Sender Bots Management → Admins and is available to every channel that has at least one admin.

                                                                                                                    Common questions

                                                                                                                    How do I become an admin of a channel?

                                                                                                                    Anyone who is a real human administrator with the Post Messages permission in your channel can be listed as an admin. The list is synced live from Telegram — connect a channel and the bot discovers its admins automatically.

                                                                                                                    Only the Main Owner (the channel creator) can manage the Admins section and change permissions. Other admins can use the features they've been granted.

                                                                                                                    Permissions & RequestsChannel Permissions
                                                                                                                    What happens if another admin of my channel activates Premium?

                                                                                                                    Premium is per channel: when any admin of a channel activates Premium, that channel's limits upgrade for everyone who uses it — other channels you have stay on their own limits.

                                                                                                                    The upgrade is automatic and needs no action from the other admins.

                                                                                                                    How Admins Share LimitsPremium
                                                                                                                    How do I request a permission I don't have?

                                                                                                                    If you tap a button you don't have access to, the bot shows "You do not have permission…" with a Request permission from the admin button underneath.

                                                                                                                    Press it, optionally add a short message explaining why you need the permission, and the Main Owner gets a Yes/No request. One request per permission per week, so think about what you ask for!

                                                                                                                    Permissions & RequestsOwnership Transfer
                                                                                                                    Do multiple admins get separate limits?

                                                                                                                    Yes — that's the whole point of the system. Every admin of the same channel shares the exact same quota: the monthly scheduled limit counts how many messages were scheduled this calendar month across all admins, and it never goes back down when messages are sent. Once the month's quota is spent, no admin can schedule more until next month (or until Premium is active for that channel).

                                                                                                                    How Admins Share LimitsLimits

                                                                                                                      Help CenterAdminsHow Admins Share Limits

                                                                                                                      How Admins Share Limits

                                                                                                                      Admins

                                                                                                                      All message-related limits are counted per channel, never per user.

                                                                                                                      Who counts: every admin of the channel — the Main Owner and everyone else — contributes to and shares one single quota. Two admins scheduling for the same channel consume the same budget.

                                                                                                                      Monthly send limit (Free): counts messages actually sent to the channel during the current calendar month — up to 100. The counter never drops when messages are deleted; it resets on the 1st of the next month, or immediately when Premium becomes active for the channel. Pending queue cap: up to 100 scheduled messages can wait to be sent at once (per channel, shared).

                                                                                                                      Pending scheduled cap: messages waiting to be sent for the channel, shared across all admins.

                                                                                                                      Recurring limit: active recurring messages for the channel, again shared.

                                                                                                                      Premium is per channel: if any admin activates Premium, the channel gets the Premium limits for everyone who uses it, while your other channels stay unaffected.

                                                                                                                      This prevents the classic free-plan loophole where several admins each connect the same channel to multiply the free limits — the quota is on the channel itself.

                                                                                                                        Help CenterAdminsPermissions & Requests

                                                                                                                        Permissions & Requests

                                                                                                                        Admins

                                                                                                                        The Main Owner manages an RBAC-style permission list for every admin of the channel.

                                                                                                                        What can be controlled:
                                                                                                                        • Scheduling messages
                                                                                                                        • Creating recurring messages
                                                                                                                        • Viewing statistics
                                                                                                                        • Leaderboard access
                                                                                                                        • Exporting data
                                                                                                                        • Managing messages (edit/delete)
                                                                                                                        • Managing sender bots

                                                                                                                        Editing: the owner opens an admin's profile and toggles permissions. Changes are collected into a draft — press Save Changes to apply them, and the bot shows a clear summary of exactly what changed before notifying the affected admin. Leaving the editor with unsaved changes prompts you to save or discard.

                                                                                                                        Immediate effect: as soon as permissions are saved, buttons for disabled features disappear from that admin's menu, and enabled ones appear. If the admin taps an old button anyway, the bot replies "You do not have permission…" with a Request permission from the admin button.

                                                                                                                        Auto-revocation: if an admin is removed from the channel in Telegram, or loses the Post Messages permission, all their bot-side permissions are revoked automatically on the next check — no manual cleanup needed.

                                                                                                                        Requests: an admin who lacks a permission can request it (optionally with an explanation). The owner receives a Yes/No request and can send back a reply when declining. Anti-spam: one request per permission per user per week. The owner can also switch off request notifications for a specific admin.

                                                                                                                          Help CenterAdminsOwnership Transfer

                                                                                                                          Ownership Transfer

                                                                                                                          Admins

                                                                                                                          Transferring the Main Owner role is deliberately protected by multiple confirmation layers.

                                                                                                                          The flow:
                                                                                                                          1. The current Main Owner opens the target admin's profile and presses Make Main Owner.
                                                                                                                          2. The bot asks the owner to type a confirmation phrase exactly (GitHub-style), e.g. "I confirm that I transfer management of [channel] to [username]".
                                                                                                                          3. After the phrase is accepted, a final confirmation button appears — the transfer is not created until it's pressed.
                                                                                                                          4. A pending transfer request is sent to the target admin, who must accept or decline it.

                                                                                                                          While pending: the current owner can cancel the request at any time, and it expires automatically after 24 hours.

                                                                                                                          On accept: the ownership swap is performed atomically — the target becomes the new Main Owner, the old owner stays as a regular admin with full permissions, and both parties are notified. At every critical step the bot re-validates that the target is still a real admin with Post Messages permission.
